title: TRIzol-Based RNA Extraction in Adult Zebrafish
author: Francisco Fuentealba-Villarroel
materials: The first step is to prepare all reagents required for the TRIzol-based RNA extraction procedure and to organise the workflow within the chemical fume hood. All solutions must be prepared using RNase-free consumables and handled with strict adherence to laboratory biosafety and chemical safety recommendations.

Preparing the Workspace and Transferring Materials to the Fume Hood 1.1.1 Decontaminate all work surfaces with an RNase-removal agent (e.g., RNase AWAY); 1.1.2 Place inside the fume hood all required materials, including TRIzol, chloroform, isopropanol, RNase-free tubes, pipette tips, and tube racks; 1.1.3 Ensure that an ice bucket, RNase-free water, and waste containers for organic solvents are available; 1.1.4 Label all RNase-free tubes in advance to avoid delays once TRIzol handling begins.

Preparation of Cleaning Supplies for iQuant Measurement 1.6.1 Set aside lint-free tissues exclusively for cleaning the measurement pedestals; 1.6.2 Confirm that the iQuant system is functioning properly and has been calibrated; 1.6.3 Ensure buffer or blanking solution is available for initial baseline measurements.

steps.title: Prepare 75% (v/v) Ethanol
steps.instruction: Prepare 100 mL of 75% (v/v) ethanol for washing.

substeps.instruction: Measure 75 mL of absolute ethanol using a graduated cylinder.
Add 25 mL of RNase-free distilled water to reach a final volume of 100 mL.
Mix gently to ensure complete homogenisation.
Transfer to an RNase-free container and store at room temperature or 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare TRIzol and Chloroform
steps.instruction: Set up TRIzol and chloroform in a fume hood due to volatility and toxicity.

substeps.instruction: Ensure sufficient TRIzol reagent is available (1 mL per 50 mg – 100 mg of tissue).
Aliquot chloroform into smaller RNase-free tubes if necessary to minimise repeated opening of the stock bottle.

steps.title: Prepare Isopropanol
steps.instruction: Ensure 100% (v/v) molecular biology–grade isopropanol is available in the fume hood.

substeps.instruction: Prepare enough volume for 500 µL per 1 mL of TRIzol used in homogenisation.

steps.title: Prepare RNase-Free Water
steps.instruction: Prepare autoclaved or commercially certified RNase-free water for resuspension and intermediate steps.

substeps.instruction: Pre-warm a small aliquot (20 µL – 50 µL per sample) in a heating block set to 55 °C – 60 °C for the final resuspension step.
Keep additional RNase-free water available on ice for intermediate steps if needed.

steps.title: Tissue Handling and Homogenisation
steps.instruction: Homogenise pooled adult zebrafish brain tissue using TRIzol.

substeps.instruction: Retrieve the pooled sample of six adult zebrafish whole brains from -80 °C only when all reagents, tubes, and equipment are prepared.
Place the frozen tissue in an RNase-free 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube kept on ice.
Add 1 mL of TRIzol for every 50 mg – 100 mg of brain tissue.
Homogenise thoroughly using a motorised pestle or homogeniser until the solution becomes uniformly lysed.
Incubate the homogenate at room temperature for 00:05:00 to permit complete dissociation of nucleoprotein complexes.

steps.title: Phase Separation
steps.instruction: Separate the RNA-containing aqueous phase from proteins and DNA using chloroform.

substeps.instruction: Add 200 µL of chloroform per 1 mL of TRIzol used in the homogenisation.
Cap the tube securely and mix by vigorous shaking for 00:00:15.
Incubate the mixture at room temperature for 00:03:00.
Centrifuge the sample at 12000 x g, 4 °C, 15 minutes.
Carefully tilt the tube to ~45° and transfer only the clear aqueous phase into a new RNase-free tube.

steps.title: RNA Precipitation
steps.instruction: Precipitate the RNA from the aqueous phase using isopropanol.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µL of isopropanol to the aqueous phase for every 1 mL of TRIzol initially used.
Mix gently by inversion and incubate at room temperature (15 °C – 30 °C) for 00:10:00.
Centrifuge at 12000 x g, 4 °C, 10 minutes.
Carefully discard the supernatant without disturbing the white gel-like RNA pellet.

steps.title: RNA Washing
steps.instruction: Wash the RNA pellet with ethanol.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 mL of 75% (v/v) ethanol per 1 mL of TRIzol used.
Vortex briefly to dislodge the pellet.
Centrifuge at 7000 x g, 4 °C, 5 minutes.
Carefully remove and discard the ethanol supernatant.
Air-dry the pellet for 00:05:00 – 00:10:00.

steps.title: RNA Resuspension
steps.instruction: Dissolve the RNA pellet in pre-warmed RNase-free water.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 20 µL – 50 µL of RNase-free water, depending on the expected yield.
Incubate the tube in a dry bath or heating block at 55 °C – 60 °C for 5 minutes to facilitate dissolution.
Briefly vortex and centrifuge to collect the solution at the bottom of the tube.

steps.title: RNA Quantification
steps.instruction: Quantify the RNA concentration and purity using iQuant.

substeps.instruction: Clean the upper and lower pedestals with a lint-free RNase-free tissue.
Apply 2 µL of blanking solution (e.g., RNase-free water) to the lower pedestal and select “Blank” on the device.
Remove the blanking solution with a clean tissue.
Pipette up to 2 µL of the RNA sample onto the pedestal and select “Measure”.
Record RNA concentration, A260/A230, and A260/A280 ratios.
Clean the pedestals thoroughly and proceed with subsequent samples.
